messages:
amira: Heads up — policy layer is adding ~12-15% p99 on hot paths. Thinking about extracting the heavy parts into an async scoring service (thin adapter pattern). Anyone tried this?

pavel: Saw the same in last perf run. Biggest offenders are region/rate-window lookups + tenant affinity evaluations.

chris: Are those lookups sync right now? Could we get wins with a short route-local cache (100ms TTL)?

amira: We have LRU caches, but misses still spike with real traffic. Also model-compat checks require up-to-date metadata that TTLs don't solve.

leila: What if policy evals split into 2 phases: inline fast-path for accept/reject and an offloaded full-scoring phase best-effort for non-critical decisions?

chris: We need deterministic outcomes for high-tier customers. Best-effort can't be allowed there unless there's a guaranteed fallback.

maria: Proposal: add "tiered evaluation" mode in the DSL. Mark stages as `critical` (sync) or `probabilistic` (async). Async stage returns score/confidence + fallback.

pavel: This implies a new adapter contract: return {decision?, score, confidence, fallback_model}. Runtime picks sync decision when confidence high otherwise use fallback. Also emit eval_latency/confidence metrics.

amira: I sketched a tiny API: `evaluate(request) -> { score: int, confidence: float, fallback: string }`. If confidence < 0.7 we immediately route to fallback.

chris: Let's avoid hard-coded thresholds. Confidence cutoff should be per-tenant config and part of rollout flags.

leila: Cache semantics matter: if adapter relies on prefetched KV, we need a clear invalidation contract for rollouts and model switches. Otherwise we serve stale compatibility decisions.

maria: I can add a `cache_invalidate(event)` hook in the control plane. Rollout pipeline emits those events when model pin changes.

ops-sre: Extra hops = more tail. If scoring is offloaded, consider colocating scoring process on the same node or using a unix socket to avoid network op.

pavel: Colocation + micro-batching looks promising. Batching window of 5-10ms could amortize cost and reduce CPU/GPU pressure.

chris: Batching increases latency for singletons. Make batch windows adaptive: aggressive batching under high QPS, minimal under tail-critical workloads.

amira: Actionable next steps: 1) proto adapter contract PR, 2) bench colocated vs remote scoring (micro-batching), 3) DSL extension for tier flags + per-tenant confidence thresholds. Volunteers?

leila: I'll own the DSL change, add examples/tests.

pavel: I'll run the bench on staging nodes, need infra to stand up colocated scoring task.

chris: I'll draft config schema for per-tenant thresholds and rollout gating signals.

amira: Thanks — if no objections I'll open an RFC follow-up tomorrow with this plan and rough perf targets (p99 budget delta <= 2% for critical paths). :thumbsup:

ops-sre: Please include expected invalidation load in the RFC. Invalidation storms can tank caches quickly.

amira: Good call — will add invalidation estimations and a backoff mechanism.

maria: One more thought — record every fallback event as an event so we can detect if async scoring causes too many fallbacks (signal to tighten thresholds).

amira: Agreed. We'll add a dashboard: fallback-rate by tenant + average scoring confidence.

chris: Sounds good. Excited to see numbers.

amira: Opening RFC tomorrow, tagging folks in the doc. Appreciate the quick sync!
